new_quiz.q: What is a Smart Object?
choices: A place in the level that tells AI characters what they can do there
A mesh that changes its shape when the player comes near
A Blueprint that spawns enemies in waves
A light that turns on when an AI character walks by
new_quiz.explain: A Smart Object holds the information needed for an interaction, for example a spot to take cover or a place to stand and wait. AI characters find it and use it.

new_quiz.q: What do Smart Objects let a designer do?
choices: Draw the NavMesh by hand
Write the animation of each AI character
Put activities into the world, where the AI finds and uses them
Replace the Behavior Tree of the AI
new_quiz.explain: The activity lives in the object in the level, not in each AI character. You add a new activity by placing one more Smart Object.

new_quiz.q: Which plugins does the quick start guide have you enable?
choices: Water, Landmass and Modeling Tools Editor Mode
Smart Objects, AI Behaviors and Gameplay Behavior Smart Objects
Movie Render Pipeline, Sequencer and Take Recorder
Niagara, Chaos and Procedural Content Generation Framework
new_quiz.explain: These three plugins bring the Smart Object system and the gameplay behaviors that agents run at a Smart Object. The editor must restart after you enable them.

new_quiz.q: What does the Smart Object Definition asset hold?
choices: The mesh and the material of the object
The walking speed of the AI character
The camera that watches the object
The slots where agents can perform a behavior
new_quiz.explain: The Smart Object Definition is a Data Asset. It describes the slots of the Smart Object and which behavior an agent runs there.

new_quiz.q: Which component do you add to the actor that should be a Smart Object?
choices: A Smart Object component, which holds the definition asset
A Character Movement component, which holds the speed
An Audio Component, which holds a sound
A Decal component, which holds a material
new_quiz.explain: The Smart Object component makes the actor known to the Smart Object system. You set the definition asset on this component.

new_quiz.q: What happens when an AI agent claims a Smart Object?
choices: The Smart Object is deleted from the level
The Smart Object moves to the agent
The Smart Object is reserved, so other agents cannot use it
The Smart Object is copied for each agent
new_quiz.explain: A claim is a reservation. It stops two agents from using the same slot at the same time.

new_quiz.q: In which order does the agent of the quick start work with a Smart Object?
choices: It uses one, then claims it, then finds it
It finds one, claims it, and then uses it
It claims one, then deletes it, then finds another
It uses one and never claims it
new_quiz.explain: One Behavior Tree task finds Smart Objects and claims one of them. A second task then uses the claimed Smart Object.

new_quiz.q: What does the Gameplay Behavior of the quick start make the agent do at the Smart Object?
choices: Spawn a wave of enemies
Open the main menu
Destroy the Smart Object
Play an animation montage
new_quiz.explain: The behavior Blueprint of the guide plays a montage on the agent. It is a simple way to see that the agent really uses the object.

new_quiz.q: You press Play, but the AI character does not walk to your new Smart Object. What do you check first?
choices: That the level has a Sky Light
That the Smart Object has a red material
That the NavMeshBoundsVolume covers the place of the Smart Object
That the Smart Object is larger than the agent
new_quiz.explain: The agent walks on the navigation mesh. If the Smart Object stands outside the NavMeshBoundsVolume, the agent has no path to it.

new_quiz.q: What must your clip or screenshots show?
choices: An AI character walking to your Smart Object and using it
The player picking up the Smart Object
The Smart Object Definition open in the editor
Two AI characters using one slot at the same time
new_quiz.explain: The proof is the working result: the agent of the guide finds the Smart Object you placed yourself, walks there and uses it.

new_quiz.q: What is a spawner?
choices: A volume that damages the player
An actor that creates enemies while the game runs
A widget that shows the number of enemies
A table that stores tuning numbers
new_quiz.explain: A spawner creates actors during play. The enemies do not have to be placed in the level by hand.

new_quiz.q: What is a wave?
choices: A group of enemies that appears together
A single enemy with a lot of health
A sound that warns the player
A path that enemies walk along
new_quiz.explain: A wave is one group of enemies that appears together. A fight is made of several waves in a row.

new_quiz.q: When does the spawner start the next wave?
choices: As soon as the first enemy of the wave appears
When the player presses the E key
At a random time
When all enemies of the current wave are destroyed, after the delay
new_quiz.explain: The next wave waits until the current one is beaten. The delay then gives the player a short pause before more enemies appear.

new_quiz.q: What does Initial Life Span set to 5 do on BP_WaveEnemy?
choices: Each enemy gets 5 health points
Each enemy waits 5 seconds before it appears
Each enemy destroys itself after 5 seconds
Each wave has 5 enemies
new_quiz.explain: Initial Life Span is how long an actor lives. With 5, each enemy removes itself after 5 seconds, so you can test waves without building combat.

new_quiz.q: Where do you set Initial Life Span?
choices: In the World Settings of the level
In the Class Defaults of BP_WaveEnemy
In the Details panel of the spawner
In the Event Graph of the Level Blueprint
new_quiz.explain: Initial Life Span is a property of the actor class. You set it in the Class Defaults of the enemy Blueprint, and every spawned enemy gets it.

new_quiz.q: Which three Instance Editable variables does BP_WaveSpawner have?
choices: The wave count, the enemies per wave and the delay
The player health, the score and the lives
The mesh, the material and the sound
The level name, the GameMode and the Kill Z
new_quiz.explain: These three numbers describe the fight: how many waves, how many enemies in each, and how long the pause between them is.

new_quiz.q: What does Instance Editable mean for these variables?
choices: They change by themselves during play
They are saved in a Data Table
They can only be changed in the graph
They can be changed in the Details panel of the placed spawner
new_quiz.explain: Each placed spawner can have its own values. You change the size and the timing of a fight by changing a few numbers, with no graph edits.

new_quiz.q: How does the spawner know that a wave is beaten?
choices: It waits a fixed time and then assumes the wave is over
It checks the health of the player
It counts the living enemies and lowers the count when an enemy is destroyed
It reads the frame rate of the game
new_quiz.explain: The spawner binds an event to On Destroyed of each spawned enemy, and that event lowers the count. When the count reaches 0, the wave is beaten.

new_quiz.q: The first wave is destroyed, but the second wave never starts. What do you check first?
choices: That the enemies have a visible mesh
That the event bound to On Destroyed of each enemy lowers the count
That the spawner is placed at the center of the level
That the delay is longer than 5 seconds
new_quiz.explain: The next wave only starts when the count of living enemies reaches 0. If the count is never lowered, the spawner waits for ever.

new_quiz.q: Where do you put the spawn points?
choices: Where the player cannot see them, for example behind cover
Directly in front of the player
Above the level, in the sky
Outside the Nav Mesh Bounds Volume
new_quiz.explain: Enemies that appear out of nothing in plain view break the illusion. Target Points behind cover let them appear unseen and then walk in.

new_quiz.q: What does the player try to do in a stealth encounter?
choices: Beat all enemies as fast as possible
Collect every pickup in the arena
Get past the enemies without being seen
Stay in one place until a timer ends
new_quiz.explain: In stealth the goal is to stay unseen. This is why the level must work in a different way from a fight.

new_quiz.q: What must cover do in a stealth level?
choices: Give the player more health
Block what the enemies see
Slow the enemies down
Mark the exit of the arena
new_quiz.explain: Cover in a stealth level is about sight. A piece of cover works when it breaks the line between an enemy and the player.

new_quiz.q: What is a patrol?
choices: A group of enemies that appears together
A place where the player is safe
A volume that covers the floor
The route that an enemy walks
new_quiz.explain: A patrol is the route an enemy walks. In a stealth level the patrols must leave a path open for the player.

new_quiz.q: How do you build a simple patrolling enemy?
choices: A Character Blueprint that walks between two Target Points with AI MoveTo
A Static Mesh that moves on a Timeline
A Pain Causing Volume that follows the player
A Widget Blueprint that shows a warning
new_quiz.explain: The enemy uses AI MoveTo to walk to one Target Point and then to the other, again and again. That gives a patrol the player can learn.

new_quiz.q: What does setting Auto Possess AI to Placed in World or Spawned do for the enemy?
choices: The enemy is hidden until the player comes near
The enemy is controlled by the keyboard of the player
An AI controller takes control of the enemy, whether it is placed or spawned
The enemy is deleted when the level starts
new_quiz.explain: A Character needs a controller to move by itself. With this setting an AI controller possesses the enemy, so AI MoveTo can work.

new_quiz.q: Why does the arena need a Nav Mesh Bounds Volume that covers the floor?
choices: It lights the floor for the enemies
It stops the player from leaving the arena
It hides the cover from the enemies
It creates the navigation mesh that AI MoveTo needs to find a path
new_quiz.explain: AI MoveTo plans its path on the navigation mesh. The volume marks the area where that mesh is built.

new_quiz.q: When does an enemy see the player in this quest?
choices: When the player is anywhere inside the arena
When the enemy faces the player and nothing blocks the line between them
When the player stands still for too long
When the player is closer than the nearest cover
new_quiz.explain: All three conditions must be true. Cover breaks the line, and the direction the enemy faces changes as it walks its patrol.

new_quiz.q: The player is seen every time at one spot of the crossing. What can you change?
choices: The cover or the patrol near that spot
The color of the floor
The name of the level
The size of the Player Start
new_quiz.explain: The quest has you change the cover and the patrols until a crossing is possible. More cover breaks the line of sight, and a different patrol opens a gap in time.

new_quiz.q: What do you mark on the screenshot taken from above?
choices: The lights and their colors
The names of the Blueprints
The patrol routes and the safe path
The frame rate at each spot
new_quiz.explain: The marked picture shows your plan: where the enemies walk and where the player can cross unseen.

new_quiz.q: What must the clip or the screenshots from Play in Editor show?
choices: The player beating all the enemies
The enemies standing still
The arena without any cover
A crossing in which the player is not seen
new_quiz.explain: A plan on a picture is not enough. The crossing in the running game proves that the safe path really works.

new_quiz.q: What is a vertical arena?
choices: An arena that is taller than it is wide and has one floor
An arena with several floors at different heights
An arena where the camera looks straight down
An arena with walls but no floor
new_quiz.explain: In a vertical arena the fight also moves up and down. Stairs, ledges and drops connect the floors.

new_quiz.q: Where do you find Max Step Height?
choices: In the World Settings of the level
In the settings of the CubeGrid tool
On the Character Movement component of BP_ThirdPersonCharacter
On the Nav Mesh Bounds Volume
new_quiz.explain: The Character Movement component holds the movement numbers of the character. Max Step Height is one of them.

new_quiz.q: What does Max Step Height tell you?
choices: How high a step the character can walk up without jumping
How high the character can jump
How tall the character is
How far the character can fall without damage
new_quiz.explain: A step that is not higher than this value can be walked up. Anything higher blocks the character until it jumps.

new_quiz.q: How do you get your jump metric?
choices: You read it on the Nav Mesh Bounds Volume
You copy it from the size of the CubeGrid
You measure the height of the character mesh
You test in Play in Editor how high a ledge the character can jump onto
new_quiz.explain: The test in the running game gives you the real number. You write it down next to Max Step Height.

new_quiz.q: What is CubeGrid?
choices: A view mode that shows the collision of meshes
A modeling tool for building simple block shapes on a grid
A plugin that creates the NavMesh
A material with a checker pattern
new_quiz.explain: CubeGrid lets you push and pull blocks on a grid. It is a fast way to graybox floors, stairs and ledges.

new_quiz.q: Where do you find the CubeGrid tool?
choices: In Landscape Mode
In Foliage Mode
In Modeling Mode
In the Place Actors panel, under Volumes
new_quiz.explain: CubeGrid is one of the tools of Modeling Mode. You switch to that mode with the mode dropdown of the editor.

new_quiz.q: What do you check every change of height against?
choices: Your step and jump metrics
The size of the Sky Light
The number of enemies
The length of the level name
new_quiz.explain: A stair must fit the step metric and a ledge must fit the jump metric. If not, the player cannot move between the floors as you planned.

new_quiz.q: A ledge that the player should jump onto is higher than your jump metric. What happens?
choices: The character climbs it more slowly
The NavMesh lifts the character onto it
The ledge is removed when the game starts
The character cannot get onto the ledge
new_quiz.explain: The jump metric is the highest ledge the character reaches. A higher ledge is a wall to the player, so you lower it or add a step.

new_quiz.q: What is the NavMesh?
choices: The mesh of the floor that the player sees
The map of where the AI can walk
The grid of the CubeGrid tool
The collision of the character
new_quiz.explain: The NavMesh marks the walkable area for the AI. You add a Nav Mesh Bounds Volume around the arena and press P to show it.

new_quiz.q: The NavMesh covers each floor but does not join the floors. What does this mean for the fight?
choices: The player cannot jump any more
The AI walks faster on each floor
The AI cannot follow the player from one floor to another
The floors lose their collision
new_quiz.explain: The AI only walks where the NavMesh is connected. It must join the floors in the places where the AI should be able to follow the player.

new_quiz.q: What is pacing in a game?
choices: How fast the character runs
How long the game takes to load
How many levels the game has
How the intensity of the game rises and falls over time
new_quiz.explain: Pacing is the change of intensity over time. Good pacing has both strong moments and quiet moments.

new_quiz.q: What happens when every fight in a row is equally hard?
choices: Players get tired or bored
Players learn the verb faster
Players find the exit sooner
Players notice the lighting more
new_quiz.explain: Without change, intensity stops feeling like anything. Players either wear out or lose interest.

new_quiz.q: What is a rest beat?
choices: The hardest fight of the level
A quiet moment between encounters
The sound that plays when an enemy dies
A checkpoint that saves the game
new_quiz.explain: A rest beat is a quiet moment. It lets the player breathe, and it makes the next peak feel stronger.

new_quiz.q: What is an intensity curve?
choices: A graph of the frame rate over time
A spline that the enemies walk along
A simple line drawing of how the intensity is planned to rise and fall
A setting on the Character Movement component
new_quiz.explain: The curve is a sketch of your pacing plan. High points are intense moments and low points are quiet ones.

new_quiz.q: What does a peak on your intensity curve stand for?
choices: A moment of high intensity, such as an encounter
A place where the level is highest
A moment when the game is paused
A point where the player has the most health
new_quiz.explain: The curve shows intensity, not height in the level. Each of the three encounters is a peak on it.

new_quiz.q: Where do the rest beats go on your curve?
choices: Only before the first encounter
Only after the last encounter
On top of each peak
Between the encounters
new_quiz.explain: You draw three encounters in a row with quiet moments between them. The curve goes up for a fight and down for a rest.

new_quiz.q: What do you note for each encounter?
choices: Which textures the arena uses
What changes compared to the one before
How long it took to build
Which Blueprint nodes it uses
new_quiz.explain: Each encounter should differ from the last one. The note says what you change, so the three fights do not feel the same.

new_quiz.q: Which three things can change from one encounter to the next in this quest?
choices: The sky, the fog or the music
The menu, the font or the language
The enemy count, the space or the verb
The camera, the lens or the exposure
new_quiz.explain: More or fewer enemies, a different space, or a different main action each change how intense a fight feels.

new_quiz.q: What is the verb of an encounter?
choices: The main action the player uses
The name of the encounter
The first word of the level description
The sound the enemies make
new_quiz.explain: The verb is the main action of the player, such as shoot or sneak. Changing the verb changes how the encounter plays.

new_quiz.q: What do the 3 lines that you send with the curve explain?
choices: Each enemy and its health
Each tool you used for the drawing
Each Blueprint in the level
Each peak and each rest
new_quiz.explain: The lines give the reason for the shape of the curve: why each peak is there and what each rest is for.
